obligations: retain the MIT copyright and permission notice in any copy or substantial portion of vitali87/code-graph-rag source that is ever redistributed

concepts (per-language security rule categorization and the specific vulnerability classes it covers) are reimplemented independently; no upstream YAML rule file, Python analyzer code, or ast-grep rule text is vendored, invoked, or executed by this pipeline
retain attribution for the rule-taxonomy concept trace in orchestration/ast-grep-rules/*.yaml header comments

ownedBoundary: per-language rule id/message/pattern text for all 7 bundled languages (python/javascript/typescript/go/rust/java/csharp)
the scan.ast-grep-security capability, its snapshot binding, scope/escape guards, and advisory-only artifact contract
no vitali87/code-graph-rag runtime dependency, no ast_grep_py binding, no Memgraph/Qdrant coupling

benefit.metric: originally-authored per-language security rule files with a passing positive/negative fixture pair each

cost.metric: pipeline-owned rule files and adapter requiring independent maintenance

update.policy: Concept-absorption source (vitali87/code-graph-rag ast_grep_rules taxonomy) verified 2026-08-25 at revision 1df81467b255d8deef330152ca4208f59bfbae08, MIT license. Before 2026-11-23, recheck whether the upstream taxonomy changed materially and whether a newly-covered language belongs in the bundled set. No upstream code is executed by this pipeline; only the categorization concept is retained.

rollback.strategy: disable the optional scan.ast-grep-security capability without changing any other artifact contract; no consumer holds authority through it, and it never gates get_gate_verdict

exit.strategy: retire the concept-absorption source reference independently; the pipeline-owned rule files and capability have no runtime dependency on vitali87/code-graph-rag and continue unaffected
replacementCriteria: every bundled rule file keeps an independent positive/negative conformance fixture
no additional language is added without its own reviewed rule file
no upstream code, YAML, or Python is ever vendored or executed

triggers: a bundled rule proves too noisy or wrong on real code and is deleted without replacement
the capability is superseded by a broader static-analysis integration
the concept-absorption source reference is no longer needed once every rule file is independently maintained
